heuristics: The walk on the (r-1)/2 inversion classes of GT is modelled as a random mapping; this is the standard rho heuristic (Brent-Pollard correction for R-adding walks), supported by the toy runs in experiment.py Part B (measured first-collision times 1.20-1.33 sqrt(N) against the model's 1.253) and used only as a heuristic.

The 1.01 per-step price is an analytic instruction ledger: one dense Fp12 multiplication (the reference operation) plus 200 charged scalar instructions for the class key, the bucket index, two 255-bit modular exponent updates, the distinguished-point test, loop and cache-miss allowances.
The 2^16 reference-operation overhead (setup pairing, one or two verification pairings, two G2 scalar multiplications, output) is charged explicitly and is 111 bits below the total.
Yielding to the class quotient can return the negation of the logarithm; both candidates are verified with a pairing, so a wrong answer is never returned as success.
The success probability claimed is the rule threshold 0.39, below the random-mapping model value 0.675 at the cap; it is not a confidence score.
limitations: Analytic complexity claim for a 2^127-step computation, not an executed attack; the rules allow an analytic argument.
Toy-scale experiment supports the mechanism and the collision-time heuristic at toy scope only, never a production complexity proof.
Only the two-class inversion quotient is claimed; the stronger 12-class Frobenius quotient used by public submissions on the sibling track is not claimed here.
Peak storage 2^78 bytes (2^67.51 distinguished-point records of 640 bytes plus a 2^29.2-byte multiplier table); memory does not enter this track's score.
